scope: Theorem 4.1 (Simultaneous lattice intersections) of the manuscript “The sharp singularity rate for biased symmetric sign matrices” (preprints/The-sharp-singularity-rate-for-biased-symmetric-sign-matrices-October-4-2026/biased-symmetric-sign-singularity.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 239 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 62c6a85b5437d9da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix D > 0 and 0 < α < 1, and put τ = ℓ−D. Typically, a nonsingular bit matrix B of size m ∈ IN has the following property. For every lattice K with BZm ⊆ K ⊆ Zm , [Zm : K] ≥ NτN , and every x ∈ Rm, |(x + K) ∩ {0, 1}m | < 2αN . The exceptional probability is uniform over the bit models specified in Section 2.
